agnostic_oa_blowup_polytope_surgery.source_support: The source says that blowing up replaces a point by a projective line and depicts this torically by replacing a triangle vertex with an interval whose length measures the new line. agnostic_oa_blowup_polytope_surgery.uncertainty: The key surgery is conveyed mainly by an unavailable figure, and several labels are OCR-damaged. The artifact distinguishes generic and special configurations qualitatively but does not supply a full deformation-theoretic analysis.

agnostic_oa_hypersurface_ambient_lift.boundary_or_failure: A generic hypersurface does not inherit the ambient torus symmetry, so the polytope alone does not represent it; the defining section and its coefficients remain essential. agnostic_oa_hypersurface_ambient_lift.interpretation: A nonsymmetric object can remain combinatorially accessible by lifting it into a higher-dimensional symmetric ambient space and representing it as a constrained zero locus. Integral polytope points organize monomial deformations, while a coefficient limit exposes a simpler union of toric boundary pieces.
agnostic_oa_hypersurface_ambient_lift.nonparaphrase_operation: When direct symmetry-based encoding fails, enlarge the ambient representation, attach an equation whose terms are indexed by the integral polytope, and compare the generic constrained object with a controlled boundary degeneration.
agnostic_oa_hypersurface_ambient_lift.source_support: The source proposes imposing equations in a higher-dimensional toric variety, treats the hypersurface equation as a line-bundle section, and assigns a monomial deformation to each integral polytope point. It notes that generic coefficients break toric symmetry and that a specified large-coefficient limit reduces the equation to a product whose zero set is the union of boundary faces.
agnostic_oa_hypersurface_ambient_lift.uncertainty: Several degree, monomial, coefficient-limit, and fiber-dimension formulas are OCR-damaged. The artifact describes the degeneration roughly, so its exact scheme-theoretic or analytic meaning is not established here.

agnostic_oa_integral_points_sections.boundary_or_failure: The lattice-point encoding depends on a chosen holomorphic line bundle and an integral normalization of the interval. The artifact supports it for the projective-line toric setting, not for arbitrary bundles, nonintegral classes, or nontoric spaces.
agnostic_oa_integral_points_sections.interpretation: Adding integral line-bundle data changes a continuous orbit-space picture into a discrete catalogue: integral points become labels for allowed global sections. The important bridge is between geometric integrality and a combinatorial index set, not the numerical evaluation of those sections.
agnostic_oa_integral_points_sections.nonparaphrase_operation: Given a continuous base equipped with integral bundle data, retain its integral lattice sites as symbolic representatives of global objects and distinguish this indexing role from computing the objects themselves.
agnostic_oa_integral_points_sections.source_support: The source identifies the bundle's first Chern data with an integral sphere volume, chooses the interval from zero to the corresponding integer, relates holomorphic sections to the integral points on that interval, and identifies those sections with successive monomials.
agnostic_oa_integral_points_sections.uncertainty: The Chern-class and section formulas contain OCR corruption, although the prose correspondence between integrality, lattice points, and sections is clear. agnostic_oa_lattice_index_singularity.boundary_or_failure: Full rank of the collapsing cycles is not enough: their primitive classes must generate the entire integral cycle lattice. The criterion presupposes the toric face-to-cycle dictionary and does not by itself diagnose nontoric, nonsimplicial, stacky, or incorrectly normalized local models.
agnostic_oa_lattice_index_singularity.interpretation: Local regularity is controlled by saturation of the vanishing-cycle lattice. Equality with the ambient lattice gives the smooth coordinate model, while finite index leaves residual finite quotient data and hence a quotient singularity.
agnostic_oa_lattice_index_singularity.nonparaphrase_operation: At each canonical zero-dimensional stratum, compare the lattice generated by the incident collapsing cycles with the full fiber-cycle lattice, interpret any finite-index gap as residual quotient structure, and use vertex locality to organize the global audit.
agnostic_oa_lattice_index_singularity.source_support: The source defines the full one-cycle lattice and the sublattice generated by cycles shrinking at a vertex, identifies their finite quotient with the group in a local quotient model, and says smoothness requires the lattices to agree. It also states that checking vertices suffices because faces adjacent to a smooth vertex are smooth.
agnostic_oa_lattice_index_singularity.uncertainty: Cycle names and example indices are OCR-damaged, and the source gives a review-level explanation rather than a formal toric proof. The finite-quotient mechanism is prose-readable, but exact example conventions require the typeset source.

agnostic_oa_open_dual_dimension_drop.boundary_or_failure: Dropping a coordinate is justified only because all dual rays in the stated local Calabi-Yau examples share the same final coordinate. Without that common affine-hyperplane condition, projection could erase scale, normal-direction, or incidence information.
agnostic_oa_open_dual_dimension_drop.interpretation: For open toric spaces, face normals are stored as rays rather than bounded polar faces. A globally fixed normal-circle contribution makes one coordinate redundant, allowing the ray data to be compressed to a finite integral point configuration one dimension lower.
agnostic_oa_open_dual_dimension_drop.nonparaphrase_operation: Convert faces into integral normal rays, identify a coordinate that is structurally constant across every ray, and only then quotient out that direction while retaining the varying lattice coordinates as the compressed dual data.
agnostic_oa_open_dual_dimension_drop.source_support: The source assigns to every face a ray through its integral normal vector and gives local examples in which the last coordinate of every such vector is one. It explains this constancy through the fixed normal-direction circle and then removes that entry to obtain lower-dimensional integral point configurations.
agnostic_oa_open_dual_dimension_drop.uncertainty: Several ray coordinates and example point lists are OCR-corrupted, so the exact configurations are not fully checkable from the artifact. The common-coordinate argument is demonstrated for the cited local models and is not presented as universal for open toric varieties.

agnostic_oa_reflexive_face_duality.boundary_or_failure: Polarity does not preserve integrality for every integral polytope; reflexivity is the additional closure condition. The construction also requires an interior origin and a lattice pairing, and dual ambient polytopes alone do not establish every proposed mirror-symmetry consequence.
agnostic_oa_reflexive_face_duality.interpretation: Reflexivity makes polar duality remain inside the same discrete category while reversing incidence dimensions: vertices and facets exchange, and intermediate faces acquire complementary dimensions. In the source, the same compatibility condition aligns the ambient line-bundle data with the Calabi-Yau hypersurface requirement.
agnostic_oa_reflexive_face_duality.nonparaphrase_operation: Apply a representation-reversing duality, test whether the result remains integral, and use that closure test to identify the admissible subclass while tracking how faces and the distinguished origin are transported.
agnostic_oa_reflexive_face_duality.source_support: The source defines the polar of an integral polytope containing the origin, observes that the polar need not be integral, and calls the integral-polar case reflexive. It states that duality exchanges vertices with boundary faces, sends a face to a complementary-dimensional face, and equates reflexivity with the relevant anticanonical line-bundle condition; the origin indexes the boundary-product deformation.
agnostic_oa_reflexive_face_duality.uncertainty: The polar inequality, dimensional notation, and line-bundle equation are OCR-damaged, so exact sign and index conventions need the typeset source. The artifact cites the mathematical correspondence but does not prove it in full.

agnostic_oa_representation_failure_audit.boundary_or_failure: A locally meaningful diagram need not encode a curve that can contract at finite moduli distance, and the existence of some alternative realization does not make it useful for extracting results. agnostic_oa_representation_failure_audit.interpretation: Representation quality splits into at least three independent questions: local consistency, support for the required global transformation, and practical inferential usefulness. agnostic_oa_representation_failure_audit.source_support: The source relates parallel external lines around a bounded interval to zero first-Chern behavior on the represented projective line and intersecting lines to negative behavior. It then invokes negativity of the normal bundle to explain why these locally sensible geometries cannot shrink as required, contrasts this with higher-dimensional toric ambient realizations using equations, and explicitly distinguishes having a brane realization from having a useful one.
agnostic_oa_representation_failure_audit.uncertainty: The relevant diagram is unavailable and bundle or Chern-class labels are OCR-damaged, so exact incidence and sign conventions need the typeset source. agnostic_oa_torus_fiber_skeleton.boundary_or_failure: The skeleton is not an unlabelled half-line or interval: it needs the circle fiber and the loci where that fiber collapses. agnostic_oa_torus_fiber_skeleton.interpretation: The orbit coordinate compresses the equivariant space while collapse labels retain the fixed-point structure that the lower-dimensional base would otherwise forget. agnostic_oa_torus_fiber_skeleton.nonparaphrase_operation: Replace an equivariant space by a base-plus-fiber description, mark every degeneration stratum, and separate intrinsic parameters such as interval length from gauge-like choices such as the coordinate origin.
agnostic_oa_torus_fiber_skeleton.source_support: The source presents the complex plane as a half-line carrying circles that shrink at its endpoint and the projective line as an interval carrying circles that shrink at both ends.
